title: Neural and radiomics score fusion estimates lung-nodule invasiveness
summary: A neural image model and radiomics SVM estimated invasive versus non-invasive or minimally invasive adenocarcinoma in surgically confirmed ground-glass lung nodules. Maximum-score fusion reached a reported AUC of 0.90 in a 127-nodule test cohort from a second center, compared with 0.83 for the neural model and 0.87 for radiomics alone. This retrospective, selected surgical cohort supports diagnostic discrimination, without establishing screening performance or clinical benefit; several fusion strategies were compared on the reported test cohort.
ai_technology: Recurrent residual U-Net, transfer-learned CNN, radiomics SVM and maximum-score fusion
organization: Taizhou University; Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center

evidence.tested: 373 pathology-confirmed nodules from323 patients:246 nodules/229 patients for training and validation at Taizhou;127 nodules/94 patients at Fudan for independent testing. Source reports maximum-fusion AUC0.90 (95%CI0.84–0.95) and accuracy80.3%; segmentation pretraining used257 LIDC-IDRI nodules.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective selected stage-I surgical nodules, multiple nodules treated independently, small cohorts and varying scanner parameters. The report compares fusion choices on the same test set, so that performance is not a separately confirmed frozen-choice estimate. No prospective clinical-utility or survival benefit.
evidence.ai_role: A recurrent residual U-Net segments nodules, a transfer-learned CNN predicts invasiveness, and an SVM classifies selected radiomics features; their prediction scores are fused.

source_review.scope: Cached original Frontiers full main text: publication metadata, cohort inclusion, segmentation and classifier Methods, fusion strategies, Results tables2/3 and limitations; supplements not independently read.
